title: What If Everyone Got Enough Sleep?

scenes.text: What if everyone got enough sleep? One study puts the price of not sleeping at hundreds of billions.
RAND researchers estimated that lack of sleep costs the U.S. economy up to four hundred eleven billion dollars a year.
That is about two point three percent of the country's entire GDP.
Japan loses up to two point nine percent. In the U.S., tired workers lose more than a million working days a year.
Sleeping under six hours a night comes with a thirteen percent higher risk of early death than seven to nine hours.
Move short sleepers up to just six to seven hours, and the U.S. could gain up to two hundred twenty-six billion dollars.
